title: Interleaved kernel arbitration causes stale KV-index reads and subtle fp drift
creator: Sofia Patel
description:
Summary: A recent change to the kernel arbitration path (priority-based dispatcher to reduce tail latency) permits prefill and decode work items from the same session to interleave on a single worker thread. Under specific timing this exposes a use-after-release of a KV-cache index pointer: decode path reads a stale kv-index while prefill is still updating metadata, leading to occasional token misalignment and small but reproducible floating-point accumulation drift in output logits when fallback kernels are used. Impact is correctness (token mismatch) on ~0.3% of requests for large-batch, long-sequence workloads in Dedicated clusters with aggressive kernel-priority enabled.

Observed behavior:
- Reproducible on stress harness with session concurrency > 24 and mix of short decode + long prefill.
- Symptoms: token duplication or shifted tokens halfway through generation (~1-4 tokens), and ~1e-6 to 1e-4 relative differences in softmax logits vs baseline.
- No GPU OOMs; worker process stays alive; issue sometimes triggers cascade of subsequent KV-miss events and increased latency for affected sessions.

Why this is critical: correctness regressions introduced by perf scheduling are high-severity: they can silently alter outputs or evaluation metrics. This ticket captures the investigation, repro, mitigation, and permanent fix for the scheduler/kv-index interaction.
reproduction_steps: 1) Deploy runtime-1.20 branch with kernel-priority-scheduler enabled (config: scheduler.mode=priority, scheduler.max_interleave=2).
2) Run harness: session_concurrency=32, batch_size=8, seq_prefill=1024, seq_decode=256, mix: 60% short-decode sessions, 40% long-prefill sessions, run for 30 minutes.
3) Collect failing traces using request-id and worker-id; compare generated tokens and logits against golden run with scheduler.mode=round-robin.
4) Observe token shift/duplication in ~0.2-0.5% of sessions and deterministic fp-diff when replaying same rng seed with fallback kernel lineage enabled.
investigation_notes: 2025-01-28 Marcus Chen: Initial bisect points to commit e3f9a4a (kernel arbitration rewrite). Reproducer attached to repro harness 'kv-stress-2025-01-28'.

2025-01-29 Sofia Patel: Heap and GPU pointer logs show kv_index pointer reused while prefill metadata write + decode read interleaved; suspect missing acquire/release around kv-index refcount in scheduler path.

2025-01-30 Keiko Tanaka: Added additional instrumentation: kv-index create/update/delete events with monotonically increasing epoch IDs. Observed decode read epoch N while prefill completed update to epoch N+1 but did not publish epoch before releasing write lock.

2025-02-02 Allan Ruiz: Floating point drift correlates with fallback kernels that use approximate softmax implementation; when stale kv-index leads to a wrong cache hit, token logits diverge slightly vs baseline and accumulate across timesteps.
2025-02-04 Marcus Chen: Stress runs with serialized arbitration (scheduler.max_interleave=0) show no failures; confirms interleaving window is the catalyst.
workaround: Disable priority-based arbitration (set scheduler.mode=round-robin or scheduler.max_interleave=0) on affected Dedicated pools; alternatively, set kv-cache.guard_epoch=true to force epoch checks (adds ~3-7% p99 latency).
temporary_mitigation_applied: 2025-02-05 Marcus Chen: Rolled out scheduler.mode=round-robin to 3 affected Dedicated clusters and increased kv-cache debug sampling to 1%. Customer-facing incidents mitigated; no new correctness reports post-rollout.
root_cause_hypothesis: Scheduler allowed interleaving of prefill update and decode read without ensuring kv-index epoch publication; combined with non-atomic pointer/epoch update this permitted a decode to read a freed or stale index when fallback kernel path was selected, exposing fp differences.
proposed_fix: 1) Make kv-index updates atomic: publish new epoch after metadata update and fence before release; add a reader-side epoch check to detect concurrent update.
2) Harden scheduler: prevent prefill and decode for same session from interleaving on same worker (session-level in-flight barrier) or ensure serialized index-update critical section.
3) Add end-to-end regression harness in CI that runs mixed prefill/decode workload with kernel-priority enabled and asserts token parity against baseline for common seeds.
4) Add unit test for epoch-based kv-index and fuzz tests for scheduler interleaving windows.
5) Optional: revert approximate softmax fallback for kernels that rely on strict KV correctness until fix is validated.
